summary: Verified 4 security fixes (SEC-001..004) via pytest against public backend. All 8 tests pass. Google OAuth rejects empty/invalid session_token, Phone OTP send-otp response does NOT leak mock_otp (SHOW_MOCK_OTP_IN_RESPONSE default false), Stripe /create-payment-intent requires auth (401 unauth, 404 for missing booking with auth), Razorpay /create-order requires auth (401 unauth). Normal login for customer@airyatra.co.in works.

minor.issue: With empty body Pydantic returns 422 (emergent_user/session_token required) before the explicit 'Session token required' 400 handler can fire. Security intent is still met (request rejected), but the reviewer-specified 400 only surfaces when emergent_user is provided with an empty session_token. Consider making emergent_user Optional so the explicit 400 message is reachable without a payload.

action_items: OPTIONAL: In EmergentAuthRequest make emergent_user Optional[dict]=None so the explicit 400 'Session token required' guard is reachable when body is completely empty (currently Pydantic 422 short-circuits). Security behavior is unchanged; this is a message-consistency improvement.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Security fix verification complete. SEC-001 Google OAuth requires session_token + server-side verification against Emergent API. SEC-002 Phone OTP hides mock_otp unless SHOW_MOCK_OTP_IN_RESPONSE=true. SEC-003 Stripe /api/stripe/create-payment-intent derives amount from booking.total_amount, enforces ownership, blocks already-paid bookings. SEC-004 Razorpay /api/razorpay/create-order requires auth + booking ownership + server-derived amount. Full-flow paid-booking test (positive path with a real booking id owned by customer) was not exercised because no seeded booking id was provided; consider adding one for regression.
